testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do both systems share in a dual air brake system?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: When checking your brakes, how much should a slack adjuster move from where it connects to the push rod?
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by pulling it. It should not move more than about one inch from where the push rod attaches. If it moves more than one inch, it needs to be adjusted or repaired.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away over time, so it cannot be relied on for emergency braking.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage allowed for a single air brake vehicle in one minute?
questions.explanation: The air brake system should not lose more than 2 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are located at each wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly get out of adjustment if they overheat from heavy use. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes engage?

options.text: You will be unable to move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to continue driving normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe air pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank that can temporarily release the spring brakes. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the best way to use your brakes on a steep downgrade?

options.text: Ride the brakes all the way down the hill.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern as you go down the hill.
Apply the brakes only near the bottom of the downgrade.
Apply steady pressure to the brake pedal all the way down the hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern as you go down the hill.
questions.explanation: On a long or steep downgrade, apply the brakes until you feel the vehicle slow down, then release them. Once your speed increases back to your target speed, repeat this process. This helps prevent brake overheating.

questions.question: What should you do before starting down a hill?
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, switch into a low gear. Gravity will pull your vehicle faster as you descend.

questions.question: Service brakes should:

options.text: Only be tested by a trained mechanic.

questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before driving. This helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: When using the controlled braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half of your usual force.
Apply the brakes so the wheels lock.
Apply the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: In controlled braking, press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering movements small.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air loss rate is 4 psi in a minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes completely until the wheels lock, release until the wheels start rolling, then repeat.
Apply the brakes about halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Fully apply the brakes, let the wheels lock, and hold the pedal down until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes completely until the wheels lock, release until the wheels start rolling, then repeat.
questions.explanation: In stab braking, fully apply the brakes until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal should activate:

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal comes on when air pressure drops below 60 psi. It may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means there are leaks in both systems.
May not affect the other system.
Is not something to worry about.
Will also affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Keep full air pressure in the brakes when the vehicle is not running.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the vehicle is not running.
Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
Do not need time to build air pressure before a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving, run the engine to build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It may also have a buzzer.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disengage the parking brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Uncouple and recouple all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system charges, test the warning signal by rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air and the warning signal should come on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is ____ below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Required when transporting both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required when transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that transports liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating while traveling uphill
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating while traveling downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When you need to stop in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep your vehicle in a straight line while braking.
Expect your vehicle to slow down more quickly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line while braking.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle going straight. You can use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep the vehicle straight while still being able to turn if needed.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air pressure enters the brake chambers. The air pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.
